input.new_string:
## [2.0.1] - 2026-08-13

Two defects a consumer of 2.0.0 can reach through the public API. Conversion output is
unchanged — every one of the 296 tests that shipped with 2.0.0 still produces the same
words.

### Fixed

- **Exception messages printed numbers in the machine's culture, so the same failure read
  differently on different machines.** `NumberOutOfRangeException` interpolated the
  offending value directly: a Turkish machine reported `1000000000000000000,5`, a Swedish
  one wrote the minus sign as U+2212 and an Arabic one used U+066B as the separator. A
  diagnostic is not localized output. Two validation messages that can interpolate a
  negative `decimalPlaces` or override key are fixed the same way. Conversion output was
  never affected; the library does no culture-sensitive formatting on that path, and a
  new test now pins that rather than leaving it true by luck.
- **`SupportedCultures` handed out the library's own cached array, so any caller could
  permanently corrupt it.** `NumberToWordsConverter.SupportedCultures` and
  `LocalizationNotFoundException.AvailableCultures` returned the live `string[]` behind a
  process-wide cache. Casting the declared `IReadOnlyList<string>` back to `string[]` and
  writing through it rewrote the supported-culture listing *and* the text of every
  subsequent "localization not found" message, for the life of the process. Both are now
  genuinely read-only.

### Changed

- `NumberToWordsConverter.SupportedCultures` and
  `LocalizationNotFoundException.AvailableCultures` still declare `IReadOnlyList<string>`,
  but their runtime type is now `ReadOnlyCollection<string>` rather than `string[]`. Code
  that cast the result to `string[]` compiled against 2.0.0 and will now throw
  `InvalidCastException`. That cast was never supported and was the defect above, but the
  change is invisible to the compiler and to package validation, so it is called out here
  rather than shipped silently.
- The build now validates the public API against the published 2.0.0 package
  (`PackageValidationBaselineVersion`), so an accidental break fails the build instead of
  reaching a consumer.

### Not in this release

Deliberately held back, so the next one has a record of why:

- A validator rule cross-checking `settings.decimalPlaces` against `numbers.scales.Length`
  would reject custom localizations that 2.0.0 accepted. Rejecting previously valid input
  is minor-version behaviour — held for 2.1.0.
- Replacing the converter's three "what follows this group" derivations with a single enum
  was proposed and rejected during review: with a `scaleKinds` entry outside the declared
  enum values — which the validator does not currently reject — the refactor changes the
  words produced. Held until the validator checks those values.
- The SDK pin in `global.json`, the GitHub Actions major bumps and .NET 6/7 test legs are
  build-only, are not part of the package, and land on `master` without a release.

## [2.0.0] - 2026-08-12

Two defects a consumer of 2.0.0 can reach through the public API. **Conversion output is unchanged** — all 296 tests that shipped with 2.0.0 still produce the same words.

### 1. Exception messages printed numbers in the machine's culture

`NumberOutOfRangeException` interpolated the offending `decimal` directly, so the same failure read differently per machine:

| Machine culture | Message said |
| --- | --- |
| `en-US` | `The number 1000000000000000000.5 is too large…` |
| `tr-TR` | `…1000000000000000000,5…` |
| `sv-SE` | minus sign as U+2212 |
| `ar-SA` | separator as U+066B, negative prefixed with U+061C |

A diagnostic is not localized output. Two validator messages that can interpolate a negative `decimalPlaces` or override key had the same problem and are fixed the same way.

Conversion output was never affected — every string comparison in the library carries an explicit `Ordinal`, both regexes are `CultureInvariant`, and the one number-to-string on the output path was already invariant. That was true only by luck; a new test now pins it.

### 2. `SupportedCultures` handed out the library's own cached array

`NumberToWordsConverter.SupportedCultures` and `LocalizationNotFoundException.AvailableCultures` returned the live `string[]` behind a process-wide `Lazy`. Reproduced against the built DLL:

```
before: en-US, es-ES, fr-FR, tr-TR
after mutating through a cast: PWNED, es-ES, fr-FR, tr-TR
exception message now: ... Available cultures: PWNED, es-ES, fr-FR, tr-TR.
```

Permanent for the life of the process, and it rewrote the text of every exception thrown afterwards. Both now hand out a `ReadOnlyCollection<string>`. The loader's own doc comment claimed cached instances were never handed out — that comment was the false premise, and it is corrected.

**Called out because no automated gate can see it:** the *runtime* type of both properties changes from `String[]` to `ReadOnlyCollection<string>`. Declared types are unchanged, so this is binary- and source-compatible and package validation is silent — but `(string[])NumberToWordsConverter.SupportedCultures` compiled against 2.0.0 and now throws `InvalidCastException`. That cast was never supported and was the defect itself.

### Also: the build now proves the no-break claim

`PackageValidationBaselineVersion` is set to `2.0.0`. The csproj comment deferring this to 2.1 was wrong — a patch release is exactly where the build should prove API compatibility rather than a human asserting it. Verified both ways: it passes against the real published 2.0.0, and making one public property `internal` fails the build with `CP0002` on all four `lib/` frameworks.

### Tests

14 new across two files. **11 of them fail without the source fixes** (verified by stashing the fixes and re-running); the other 3 pin the culture-independence of conversion output, which was already true.

- `InvariantMessageTests` — runs under `tr-TR`, `sv-SE`, `ar-SA`, `de-DE`. Asserts only on the invariant text, never on what the hostile culture produces, so NLS-vs-ICU differences on the net48 leg cannot make it flaky. Its own xunit collection with parallelization disabled, and `CurrentCulture` restored in a `finally`.
- `CachedListImmutabilityTests` — the cast vector and the `IList<string>` write vector, on both the listing and the exception, plus that a caller-supplied array is snapshotted.

310 pass on net9.0, net8.0 and net48.

### Deliberately not in this release

Reviewed and held back, recorded in the changelog:

- **A `decimalPlaces` vs `scales.Length` validator rule** — correct and arithmetically verified, but it rejects custom localizations that 2.0.0 accepted. Rejecting previously valid input is minor-version behaviour → 2.1.0.
- **Collapsing the converter's three "what follows this group" derivations into one enum** — proposed, then rejected during review. With a `scaleKinds` entry outside the declared enum values (which the validator checks the length of but not the values of), the refactor **changes the words produced**: `ONE THOUSAND` → `UN THOUSAND` on 3 of 4 probe cases. Held until the validator rejects undefined enum values.
- **`global.json` rollForward, GitHub Actions major bumps, .NET 6/7 test legs** — build-only, not part of the package. They land on `master` separately, where CI can prove them with no release riding on the result.
EOF

content.text:
**PR #5 açık** — https://github.com/keparlak/NumWordify/pull/5 — CI koşuyor (ubuntu yeşil, windows sürüyor).

## Ne uygulandı

Sekiz maddeden **ikisi** 2.0.1'e girdi. Uzlaştırıcı diğer altısını kesti ve gerekçeleri sağlamdı:

**Giren 1 — Tanı mesajları makine kültürüyle sayı basıyordu.** `NumberOutOfRangeException` değeri doğrudan interpolasyona sokuyordu: Türkçe makinede `1000000000000000000,5`, İsveççede eksi işareti U+2212, Arapçada ayraç U+066B. Tanı mesajı yerelleştirilmiş çıktı değildir. Negatif `decimalPlaces` veya override anahtarı taşıyabilen iki validator mesajı da aynı şekilde düzeltildi.

**Giren 2 — `SupportedCultures` kütüphanenin kendi cache dizisini dağıtıyordu.** DLL'e karşı yeniden üretildi: cast'leyip yazınca hem liste hem de **sonrasında fırlatılan her istisnanın metni** proses ömrü boyunca bozuluyor. İkisi de artık `ReadOnlyCollection`.

**Ek — Sekiz incelemenin de kaçırdığı şey.** Uzlaştırıcı `PackageValidationBaselineVersion`'ı buldu: csproj'daki yorum "2.1'den itibaren ayarla" diyordu, ama 2.0.1 karşılaştırılacak ilk baseline'a sahip sürüm. Ayarlandı ve **iki yönlü doğrulandı** — yayınlanmış gerçek 2.0.0'a karşı geçiyor, ve bir public property'yi kasten `internal` yapınca dört `lib/` hedefinde de `CP0002` ile build kırılıyor. "Public API kırılmadı" iddiası artık insan beyanı değil, build çıktısı.

**Testler:** 14 yeni, ikisi `tr-TR`/`sv-SE`/`ar-SA`/`de-DE` altında koşuyor. Kaynak düzeltmelerini stash'leyip koşturdum: **11'i kırmızı yanıyor.** Geçen 3'ü zaten doğru olan "çıktı kültürden bağımsız" özelliğini pinliyor — o da şu ana kadar hiçbir şeyle korunmuyordu. 310 test net9.0/net8.0/net48'de yeşil.

## Kesilenler — ve biri gerçek bir kurtarma

En değerlisi: **`Following` enum refactor'ü reddedildi.** İnceleme onu 384 sentetik locale üzerinde 489.608 çıktıyla "byte-for-byte özdeş" diye savunmuştu. Uzlaştırıcı korpüsün yalnızca `Adjective`/`Noun` değerlerini taradığını fark etti — ama `scaleKinds` public bir enum dizisi ve validator sadece **uzunluğunu** kontrol ediyor, değerlerini değil. `(ScaleKind)7` ile master ve refactor yan yana koşturulduğunda 4 vakanın 3'ü ayrışıyor: `ONE THOUSAND` → `UN THOUSAND`. Bir patch sürümünde değişmiş dönüşüm çıktısı. Ezici görünen kanıt, karşı örneği dışlayan bir uzayda ezici olduğu için ezici görünüyormuş.

Diğerleri: `decimalPlaces` doğrulama kuralı (2.0.0'ın kabul ettiği modelleri reddediyor → minor davranışı, 2.1.0'a); loader case-sensitivity (tüketici için erişilemez, mevcut testler zaten doğru anda kırılıyor); net6/net7 test bacakları (gerekçesi kültür duyarlılığıydı, ama kültür denetimi kütüphanede kültür duyarlı hiçbir işlem kalmadığını kanıtladı); `global.json` ve Actions v5 (ikisi de publish.yml'i etkiliyor — 2.0.0'ı başarıyla yayınlayan hattı, yayın günü, kozmetik bir uyarı için değiştirmek yanlış takas). Son ikisi tag'den sonra master'a ayrı PR olarak inecek.

Diff şu an dört mercekten çekişmeli incelemeye girdi — her bulgu iki bağımsız çürütücüye gidiyor, biri teknik biri sürüm merceğinden, ve belirsizlikte varsayılan "çürütüldü". Sonrasında bir eksiklik eleştirmeni incelemenin kendisini denetleyecek. Sonuç gelince CI ile birlikte değerlendirip merge ve v2.0.1 tag'ine geçerim.

SHIP RECOMMENDATION: SHIP

MUST FIX:

REASONING TAIL:
lease on its own merits: it is not self-inflicted-only. Any code anywhere in the process — a transitive dependency, a plugin, a misbehaving DI container doing array fixups — can permanently corrupt the culture listing and the text of every subsequent exception. That is a cross-library corruption vector reachable through a documented public property, and it is exactly what a patch is for. The invariant-messages fix alone would not have justified a release; bundled with this one, both go out.

Third, this release installs the PackageValidationBaselineVersion gate. Every later release benefits from it, and the earlier it lands the more history it covers. That is a real reason to prefer a small release now over a larger one later.

On the SemVer label: a purist can argue that InvalidCastException where 2.0.0 worked is a breaking change and belongs in 2.1.0 or 3.0.0. I disagree, and the diff's own reasoning is right. The compile-time and binary surface is unchanged and ApiCompat is silent, which I verified — the baseline passes against the real published package while catching a genuine public-to-internal flip. The affected pattern was reading and writing through a collection the API declared as read-only. .NET convention treats that as a fix. Calling it 2.1.0 would also be worse than misleading here: a minor version implies new capability and there is none, and the changelog's "Not in this release" section explicitly reserves 2.1.0 for the validator rule that will reject previously valid input. The version numbers are being used deliberately.

One operational caution that follows from this release, not a code change: after 2.0.1 goes out there will be a temptation to remove 2.0.0 from nuget.org because it carries a live defect. Unlisting is safe — the baseline is fetched as an exact-version PackageDownload, and exact-version restore resolves unlisted packages. Actual deletion (which requires contacting nuget.org support) would break `dotnet restore` for the entire repository, including the tag build for 2.0.2. Worth knowing before anyone acts on the impulse.

WHAT MY OWN REVIEW DID NOT COVER

I ran only the Windows leg. The CI matrix also runs ubuntu-latest, where CultureInfo is ICU-backed rather than NLS. The new tests assert only on invariant text and on resource-derived Turkish output (the library performs no casing anywhere — I grepped for ToUpper/ToLower and there are none, so the "BİN İKİ YÜZ..." assertion comes from the JSON, not from culture), so the risk is low, but I did not execute it. I also did not test net6.0/net7.0 at runtime; the test project targets only net9.0/net8.0/net48, so those two TFMs are compile-verified only — a pre-existing gap the changelog acknowledges as deferred, not something this diff introduced.

VERDICT

Nothing in this diff blocks a release. The two fixes are correct, minimal, and demonstrably do not touch conversion output. The build gate they added works. The timing argues for shipping rather than waiting. SHIP.

directions on the same thing: the comment said more than the code did.

`availableCultures as ReadOnlyCollection<string> ?? ...ToArray()` skipped the
copy when the argument was already a read-only collection. But
ReadOnlyCollection is a read-only *view*, not an immutable collection — the
array or list behind it stays writable through the reference the caller kept.
Demonstrated: pass a ReadOnlyCollection over a List, mutate the List, and the
exception's AvailableCultures changes after the exception was thrown, while its
Message still reads the old values. The library's own call site was never
affected, so this closes a hole in the public constructor rather than a live
defect. Now always copies; the comment now describes what the code does.

The rest is honesty about coverage, not behaviour:

- The invariant-message tests do not all discriminate on both legs. .NET
  Framework uses NLS, where no installed culture formats a negative integer
  differently from invariant and ar-SA formats decimals identically to it, so
  on net48 the ar-SA rows and the whole validation-message test pass with or
  without the fix. Stated in the remark instead of implied away.
- Conversion_output_does_not_depend_on_the_machine_culture pins the conversion
  path only. Localizations are cached process-wide, so the parse path was
  already exercised under whatever culture ran first and is out of reach from a
  test. Said so.
- Pow10's invariant fix had no test at all — reverting it left all 310 green.
  Now covered, by the mutate-after-handover path that reaches it.
- Noted in the csproj that PackageValidationBaselineVersion is hand-maintained
  and must name a version that exists on nuget.org.

312 pass on net9.0, net8.0 and net48.

build: unblock newer SDKs and move off the Node 20 actions

Not part of the package — none of these files are packed, so there is nothing
to release. They were deliberately held out of 2.0.1 because two of them touch
publish.yml, and rewriting the release pipeline on the day of a release is the
wrong trade.

global.json pinned 9.0.100 with rollForward latestFeature, which never crosses
a major version. A contributor whose only SDK is .NET 10 could not run restore,
build or test at all — verified against a root exposing only 10.0.204: "A
compatible .NET SDK was not found. Installed SDKs: <empty>". latestMinor does
NOT fix this; it fails identically. Only latestMajor crosses the boundary, and
it keeps the 9.0.100 floor: a root exposing only 8.0.424 is still correctly
refused. Verified on this machine after the change — dotnet --version now
resolves 10.0.204, the library builds all five target frameworks with zero
warnings under TreatWarningsAsErrors, and 312 tests pass on net9.0, net8.0 and
net48.

allowPrerelease defaults to true, which combined with latestMajor would let a
maintainer with a preview SDK installed silently build, and publish, on it.
Turned off.

The original pin was justified as stopping a new SDK band from turning a
release build red. That job is already done by AnalysisLevel in
Directory.Build.props, which travels with the repo and is independent of which
SDK resolves — confirmed by the zero-warning build on SDK 10.

actions/checkout v4 and setup-dotnet v4 target Node 20 and every run warned
that the runner was forcing them onto Node 24. Bumped to v7 and v6, the current
majors. NuGet/login@v1 already declares node24 and is left alone.

Also corrects the ci.yml comment justifying the Windows leg. It claimed the
library does culture-sensitive string work; the audit behind 2.0.1 established
the opposite — every comparison carries an explicit Ordinal and there is no
casing anywhere. The leg is still needed, for net48 and for NLS coverage, which
is what the comment now says.
EOF
